Group: issue #48 alone; no duplicates. Verdict: easy-call. Moderate implementation and testing effort; narrow internal two-way change, with no public API or schema change needed.

At upstream a27b439b2dc96cf0bd0bf8f76ab33ff6d5664b25, KeyBasedPagination builds lexicographic disjunctions using greaterThan/lessThan and ordinary equality prefixes. It never reads null precedence or branches on null values. SQL null semantics explain exclusion of trailing nulls, inability to advance from a null boundary, and failure through repeated-null prefixes. This is source evidence; no executable RED or affected-release verification has yet run.

Relevant locations: hibernate-core/src/main/java/org/hibernate/query/internal/KeyBasedPagination.java, hibernate-core/src/main/java/org/hibernate/query/internal/SelectionQueryImpl.java, and hibernate-core/src/test/java/org/hibernate/orm/test/paging/keybased/KeyBasedPagingTest.java.

Resolve effective FIRST/LAST consistently with SQL ordering: explicit precedence, configured session-factory default, then dialect getNullOrderingSupport().getDefaultOrdering() with direction. Resolve original ordering before backwards traversal, then invert direction and effective null placement locally. NamedAttributeOrder.reverse() currently reverses direction while preserving explicit null precedence; do not change that public contract to fix pagination.

For a null boundary, the strictly-after branch is IS NOT NULL for nulls first and false for nulls last. For a non-null boundary, retain the directional comparison and include IS NULL when nulls sort last. Prefix equality must use IS NULL for null boundaries. Preserve subsequent tie-breaker branches and the existing AND with the original query restriction.

Use a focused sibling of KeyBasedPagingTest. First observe the reporter regression fail in Actions on unchanged production. Then verify explicit FIRST/LAST, ascending/descending, repeated nulls and unique tie-breakers, size 1/2 boundaries, backward round trips, configured/dialect defaults and existing WHERE restrictions. Run adjacent key-pagination tests and formatting on the exact fixed revision. Existing tests cover non-null traversal, composite keys, restrictions and query reuse, but not explicit null precedence.

Open implementation question: normalize effective ordering in the session-aware caller without requiring unavailable session-factory services during SQM creation. No human decision or reporter clarification is required. CONTRIBUTING.md was read; CONTEXT.md, .sandcastle/CODING_STANDARDS.md and docs/adr were absent. No code changed and no build/tests run.
